invests.text: PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 5.7S 68.1E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 8.1S 69.3E, APPROXIMATELY 192 NM WEST- SOUTHWEST OF DIEGO GARCIA. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS AN ELONGATED REGION CYCLONIC TURNING, WITH DEEP CONVECTION DEVELOPING IN THE SOUTHEASTERN QUADRANT ALONG AN ASYMPTOTE OF LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE. AN EARLIER SCATTEROMETER PASS REVEALED A TROF-LIKE FEATURE, WITH A LOW LEVEL CIRCULATION (LLC) BEGINNING TO CONGEAL IN THE SOUTHEASTERN END OF THE TROF. ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS ARE MARGINAL, WITH MODERATE TO HIGH (20-25 KNOTS) OF SOUTHEASTERLY SHEAR, WARM SSTS AND GOOD EQUATORWARD OUTFLOW ALOFT. GLOBAL AND ENSEMBLE MODELS ARE SPLIT, WITH THE GFS SHOWING A BRIEF PERIOD OF CONSOLIDATION AND INTENSIFICATION WHILE REMAINING BELOW WARNING TRESHOLD, WHILE THE ECMWF DOES NOT SHOW DEVELOPMENT OF THE SYSTEM. GEFS AND GOOGLE DEEPMIND ENSEMBLES BOTH INDICATE A SOUTHWARD TRAJECTORY WITH A MODERATE CHANCE OF DEVELOPMENT TO MINIMAL TROPICAL CYCLONE STRENGTH OVER THE NEXT 24 TO 36 HOURS. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1006 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS LOW.

PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 7.1S 76.0E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 8.9S 78.6E, APPROXIMATELY 376 NM EAST- SOUTHEAST OF DIEGO GARCIA. ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE IMAGERY (MSI) DEPICTS A COMPACT, DEVELOPING LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION (LLC) WITH FORMATIVE CURVATURE BANDING AROUND THE EASTERN PORTION OF THE SYSTEM AND MODERATE CONVECTION. THE SYSTEM HAS BEEN REANALYZED AFTER RECEIPT OF MULTIPLE MICROWAVE PASSES INCLUDING A 232319Z GMI 37 GHZ AND 240016Z SSMIS 37 GHZ IMAGE WHICH SHOWED THE LOW LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) TO THE EAST OF THE FLARING CONVECTION VICE SOUTHWEST. TENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS FAVORABLE CONDITIONS WITH LOW TO MODERATE (20-15) VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) AND WARM (28-29 C) SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES AND WEAK EQUATORWARD AND POLEWARD OUTFLOW. GLOBAL MODELS ARE SPLIT, WITH GFS DEPICTING MINIMAL DEVELOPMENT, WHILE ECMWF DOES NOT SHOW THE SYSTEM DEVELOPING FURTHER. BOTH MODELS INDICATE A GENERAL SOUTH- SOUTHWESTWARD TRACK OVER THE NEXT 24-36 HOURS. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1006 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS HIGH. SEE REF A (WTXS21 PGTW 240400)FOR FURTHER DETAILS.
